title: Circular Letter DHCQ 18-6-679: Schedule II-V controlled substances in long-term care facility emergency kits
subtopic: Emergency medication kits: controlled substance list
rule_summary: Department of Public Health Circular Letter DHCQ 18-6-679 (June 15, 2018), jointly issued by the Bureau of Health Care Safety and Quality and the Drug Control Program and Board of Registration in Pharmacy through the Bureau of Health Professions Licensure, attaches the revised list of Schedule II-V controlled substances that long-term care facilities are permitted to store on their premises in a locked emergency kit, and supersedes Circular Letter DHCQ 06-10-467 (October 18, 2006). The list was developed under 105 CMR 150.008(E)(1). Actual contents are determined by each facility within the Department's framework, which allows a choice of federally controlled analgesic and sedative/anticonvulsant medications in Schedules II-V up to a maximum number of units per facility based on licensed bed capacity, in a 3:1 ratio of analgesics to sedatives/anticonvulsants: analgesics (CII-CV) 45 units for <50 beds, 60 for 51-100 beds, 75 for 101-150 beds and 90 for >150 beds; sedatives/anticonvulsants (CII-CV) 15, 20, 25 and 30 units in the same bands. Each facility should develop its own formulary in conjunction with a single pharmacy provider of its own choosing and develop policies and procedures, including measures for controlled substance accountability and security, subject to review; facilities are not required to have all items or the maximum quantity. Each unit must be tamper evident/resistant, in an individually packaged, single dose form. Facilities that wish to store Schedule VI controlled substances for emergency doses must comply with the requirements for procurement, storage, dispensing, administration, recording and disposal of those substances; their storage must comply with facility policies and procedures under 105 CMR 150.008 and with federal and state law, and their use must be monitored by the facility's Quality Assurance and Assessment Committee. DPH approves the use of automated dispensing devices by long-term care facilities in place of the traditional locked boxes for Schedule II-V controlled substances in emergency kits, provided all relevant regulations and guidance requirements are met. Emergency kit practices, policies and procedures may be reviewed at any time by Bureau of Health Care Safety and Quality or Drug Control Program staff.
exam_relevance: Tests the bed-capacity unit caps for each category, the single-dose tamper-evident packaging, the Schedule VI conditions and the automated dispensing device substitution.

common_confusions: The caps are per category and per facility, not per drug.
A facility need not stock every item or the maximum quantity.
The printed bands are <50 and 51-100 beds; the list does not print a band for exactly 50 beds.
